recommendations.recommendation: Treat war as a matter of life and death for the state and study it thoroughly.
recommendations.rationale: War is the ground of death and life and the road to survival or ruin.

recommendations.recommendation: Before fighting, compare yourself with the enemy on the Way, heaven, terrain, command, and method.
recommendations.rationale: Many calculations in the temple predict victory; few predict defeat; none at all is worse.

recommendations.recommendation: Use deception: appear unable when able, inactive when active, far when near.
recommendations.rationale: All warfare is based on deception; misleading the enemy lets you strike where he is unprepared.

recommendations.recommendation: Avoid prolonged campaigns and seek swift victory.
recommendations.rationale: No state has ever benefited from long war; it exhausts treasury, dulls weapons, and invites neighboring rivals to attack.

recommendations.recommendation: Feed your army from the enemy's supplies.
recommendations.rationale: 1 cartload taken from the enemy equals 20 sent from home.

recommendations.recommendation: Aim to subdue the enemy without fighting; attack his strategy first, then his alliances, then his army, and cities only last.
recommendations.rationale: Winning 100 battles is not the highest skill; breaking resistance without battle and taking things intact is.

recommendations.recommendation: Know the enemy and know yourself.
recommendations.rationale: Then you will not be endangered in 100 battles; knowing only one side gives even odds, knowing neither means certain defeat.

recommendations.recommendation: First make yourself invulnerable, then wait for the enemy to become vulnerable.
recommendations.rationale: Invulnerability depends on oneself, while the opportunity to win is supplied by the enemy; victorious armies win first and then fight.
recommendations.argued_against: those who fight first and then seek victory

recommendations.recommendation: Combine direct and indirect forces in endlessly varied ways.
recommendations.rationale: Like 5 notes or 5 colors, their combinations are inexhaustible and keep the enemy off balance.

recommendations.recommendation: Strike the enemy's weak points, avoid his strong ones, and stay formless like water.
recommendations.rationale: Water avoids heights and flows to low ground; an army without fixed form adapts to the enemy and cannot be anticipated.

recommendations.recommendation: Adapt your maneuvers to the terrain and circumstances.
recommendations.rationale: Each kind of ground calls for a different response, and a general who does not grasp these variations cannot use his troops well.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not interfere with a capable general's conduct of the army.
recommendations.rationale: A ruler who hobbles the army or meddles in its administration causes confusion and gives victory to the enemy.

recommendations.recommendation: Disregard some of the sovereign's commands when battlefield conditions require it.
recommendations.rationale: There are roads not to follow, armies not to attack, and cities not to besiege, and orders that would cause defeat.
recommendations.conditions: when circumstances make the order harmful

recommendations.recommendation: Avoid the 5 dangerous faults: recklessness, cowardice, hot temper, touchy honor, and excessive concern for your men.
recommendations.rationale: Each fault can be exploited by the enemy and leads to the ruin of the army and the death of the general.

recommendations.recommendation: Never go to war out of anger or resentment.
recommendations.rationale: Anger can turn back to gladness, but a ruined state cannot be restored nor the dead brought back to life.
recommendations.conditions: move only when there is advantage
recommendations.argued_against: rulers and generals acting from passion

recommendations.recommendation: Treat your soldiers like beloved sons, but enforce discipline.
recommendations.rationale: Soldiers so treated will follow into deep valleys and die with you, but indulgence without authority makes them like spoiled children, useless.
recommendations.conditions: kindness must be backed by firm command

recommendations.recommendation: Make rewards and punishments clear and consistent.
recommendations.rationale: Clarity in rewards and punishments is one of the measures that decides which side will win.

recommendations.recommendation: Treat captured soldiers well and bring them over to your side.
recommendations.rationale: This uses the conquered enemy to increase one's own strength.

recommendations.recommendation: Leave a surrounded enemy a way out and do not press a desperate foe.
recommendations.rationale: An enemy with no escape fights to the death.

recommendations.recommendation: Place your own troops where they cannot retreat so they fight with full force.
recommendations.rationale: Soldiers on death ground with no escape fight hardest and survive.

recommendations.recommendation: Use spies of all 5 kinds and reward them generously.
recommendations.rationale: Foreknowledge cannot come from spirits or omens, only from people; begrudging spies a small cost while war costs so much is inhumane.
recommendations.argued_against: reliance on divination, and stinginess toward spies

recommendations.recommendation: Rely on your own readiness rather than on the hope that the enemy will not come.
recommendations.rationale: Being unassailable depends on oneself, not on the enemy's restraint.

recommendations.recommendation: Act only when there is clear advantage, and fight only when the situation is critical.
recommendations.rationale: The enlightened ruler is prudent and the good general cautious; this keeps the state secure and the army intact.
